subject: humanities
passage: Papel picado, which means "perforated paper" in Spanish, is a Mexican folk art in which designs are cut into thin tissue paper. Artisans stack dozens of sheets and cut through them all at once with small chisels. <u>The finished sheets are strung together into colorful banners that are hung over streets and doorways during celebrations such as the Day of the Dead.</u> Because the paper is so delicate, the banners usually last only a short time.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?

choices.A: It explains how artisans cut designs into stacks of paper.
choices.B: It suggests that the banners are made to be kept for many years.
choices.C: It describes how the finished cut paper is displayed and used.
choices.D: It argues that papel picado is the most popular art form in Mexico.

explanation.why: The sentence before the underlined one explains how the designs are cut. The underlined sentence moves to what happens next: the sheets become banners "hung over streets and doorways during celebrations." Its role is to show how the finished paper is used.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The cutting is described in the sentence before; the underlined sentence is about the finished sheets.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The last sentence says the banners "usually last only a short time," the opposite of this choice.
explanation.C: Correct. The sentence tells how the sheets are strung into banners and hung during celebrations.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text never compares papel picado with other Mexican art forms.
